articles.title: Elumelu Acquires Additional $70m Seplat Shares, Raises Stake to 22.05%
articles.snippet: Elumelu Acquires Additional $70m Seplat Shares, Raises Stake to 22.05% Business Post Nigeria
articles.text:
Economy
Elumelu Acquires Additional $70m Seplat Shares, Raises Stake to 22.05%
Published 2 seconds ago
on 17/11/2026
By Adedapo Adesanya
By Adedapo Adesanya
Nigerian businessman, Mr Tony Elumelu, has acquired an additional $70 million stake in Seplat Energy Plc through his energy investment firm, Heirs Energies Limited, increasing its shareholding in the energy firm to 22.05 per cent.
The latest acquisition involved approximately 5.9 million shares, representing about one per cent of Seplat, Bloomberg reported, citing a spokesperson for Heirs Energies.
The transaction marks another increase in Mr Elumelu’s investment in the Nigerian energy company, following a similar acquisition in September and an initial purchase of a 20 per cent slice in December 2025.
In October, Heirs Energies acquired an additional six million shares, representing one per cent of Seplat, for approximately £53.22 million (about N94 billion), raising its shareholding to 21.07 per cent at the time.
The initial acquisition involved about 120.4 million shares purchased from French energy company Maurel & Prom for about $500 million.
The latest investment comes as Heirs Energies pursues plans to expand its operations and increase its stake in Seplat.
The company’s chief executive, Mr Osa Igiehon, said in an interview last month that increasing its holding in Seplat aligns with its growth strategy, which also includes raising oil production to 100,000 barrels per day by the end of the decade.
Meanwhile, Mr Elumelu is expected to assume the position of Chairman of Seplat on January 1, 2027, succeeding Mr Udoma Udo Udoma, who is due to retire from the organisation’s board on December 31, 2026.

articles.title: BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
articles.snippet:
BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $62.9 million for global support of energy automation and fuel-storage safety systems.
The post BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:39 AM
BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $62.9 million for global support of energy automation and fuel-storage safety systems.
The Rockville, Maryland-based contractor will provide sustainment for operational technology, automatic tank gauging, independent alarm systems, and overfill-protection equipment.
The Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard are identified as customers under the contract. The broad customer group reflects the use of fuel-management and storage systems throughout military installations and operational locations.
The five-year contract includes no option periods and has a performance completion date of November 9, 2031. Its stated $62.9 million value is the maximum IDIQ ceiling rather than a guaranteed payment to BAE Systems.
The government will issue orders for required products or services over the performance period. The announcement does not identify an initial task order, guaranteed minimum, or specific amount obligated when the IDIQ contract was awarded.
Fiscal 2027 defense working capital funds are identified as the applicable appropriation. Future orders and obligations will depend on customer requirements, available funding, and the contract’s ordering procedures.
The procurement was competitive, with four responses received. The Defense Logistics Agency Contracting Services Office in Columbus, Ohio, is the contracting activity for contract SP4706-27-D-0002.
Automatic tank gauges help monitor fuel levels and related storage conditions. Independent alarms and overfill-protection equipment can reduce the risk of spills, equipment damage, environmental incidents, and operational interruptions.
Operational technology sustainment may include maintenance, technical support, configuration management, repair, replacement, and other services needed to keep these systems functioning. The government announcement does not provide a more detailed breakdown of individual tasks.
The contract gives multiple military services and the Coast Guard a common mechanism for obtaining global support. BAE Systems will be eligible to receive orders up to the ceiling during the five-year period, but actual contract revenue will depend on the number and value of orders placed.

articles.text:
FHLBank Chicago: $62 Million Affordable Housing Grants To Support 1,786 Homes Across Illinois And Wisconsin
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:29 AM
FHLBank Chicago: $62 Million Affordable Housing Grants To Support 1,786 Homes Across Illinois And Wisconsin
The Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago has awarded $62 million through its 2026 Affordable Housing Program General Fund to finance 47 affordable housing projects in Illinois and Wisconsin. The funding will support the acquisition, rehabilitation, and construction of 1,786 affordable housing units across the two states.
The awards include an additional $10 million approved by FHLBank Chicago’s Board of Directors to expand support for affordable housing development.
The grants are intended to address housing affordability challenges as development costs and constrained housing supply continue to affect communities.
FHLBank Chicago operates as a regional member-owned cooperative within the Federal Home Loan Bank System.
Its member institutions include commercial banks, credit unions, insurance companies, savings institutions, and community development financial institutions.
The Affordable Housing Program provides grants to support projects sponsored through participating member institutions.
Applications are submitted by housing developers, government organizations, public housing authorities, tribally designated organizations, and other eligible participants.
The funding helps bridge gaps between the cost of providing affordable housing and the financing available through other sources.
The 2026 awards cover projects involving different housing needs and development approaches.
One recipient is Reclaiming Chicago NFP, which received support for the construction of 24 affordable single-family homes on vacant city-owned lots.
The homes will be developed across four Chicago neighborhoods: Back of the Yards, Roseland, North Lawndale, and Washington Park.
The project is sponsored by First Eagle Bank, a member of FHLBank Chicago.
It is part of an initiative organized by United Power for Action and Justice, a coalition that brings together civic and religious organizations.
Five nonprofit development partners are participating in the effort.
The project is intended to expand opportunities for homeownership while returning vacant properties to productive residential use.
First Eagle Bank has also provided a $1 million interest-free loan to support the development.
The combination of financing and grant support is intended to help move the project toward construction.
Another award will support Milwaukee Development Corporation’s conversion of a former hospital into affordable apartments.
The project will create 124 residences for adults ages 55 and older.
Of those units, 25 will be designated as supportive housing for residents with disabilities.
Jewish Family Services will provide on-site services to eligible residents.
Associated Bank is sponsoring the project through the Affordable Housing Program.
The redevelopment is intended to preserve a historic building while introducing additional affordable housing options for older adults.
Projects like these illustrate the program’s support for both new construction and the reuse of existing properties.
Since the Affordable Housing Program General Fund began in 1989, FHLBank Chicago has allocated more than $630 million in grants through the end of 2025.
These investments have helped provide housing for more than 85,000 households.
